title: Lost Your Job or Laid Off? What to Do First to Get Hired Faster
description:
If you lost your job, were laid off, or are suddenly job searching, updating your resume while stressed is brutal. Your brain goes blank, you forget your wins, and a simple resume update turns into an overwhelming, all-day spiral.

That’s why I teach every client to use a simple job search tool that keeps track of your wins, results, and proof as they happen — so you’re never starting from scratch again.

I call it a brag bank.

In this video, I show you exactly how to build a brag bank so your resume is faster to write, interviews are easier to prep for, and your job search feels calmer and more strategic — even during a layoff or unexpected career change.

You’ll learn:
• How to track career wins and accomplishments the easy way
• How to organize results, impact, and proof hiring managers care about
• Why resumes sound generic when you rely on memory
• How to stay “layoff-ready” without panic-applying
• How to use AI to turn messy notes into strong, results-driven resume bullet points

AI can make resume writing faster — but only if you give it real content. I’ll show you how to combine your brag bank with smart AI prompts so you get polished, tailored resume bullets instead of generic fluff.

Whether you’re navigating a layoff, preparing for a career move, or improving your resume strategy, this system helps you get hired faster with less stress.

transcript: When you suddenly find your job searching, a layoff, or something unexpected, updating your resume while you're stressed and trying to find another job is brutal. Your brain goes blank. You forget your wins, and a simple update turns into an overwhelming all day project. In this video, I'm going to show you a simple system that fixes that. So, your resume is faster and easier to write, and interviews are easier to prep for, and you're never starting from scratch again, especially when you're already stressed out in job searching. Hi, I'm Kate Kersner, career strategist and your career bestie. And this is one of the easiest, highest impact habits I teach my clients. It's called a brain bank. And before you picture something fancy or complicated, it's really not. A brain bank is not your resume. It's not polished. It's not formatted. And it's not even something you need to share with anyone if you don't want to. It's just a messy running document where you dump your wins as they happen. projects you've finished, a problem you've fixed, time you've saved, money you saved, a process you cleaned up, a customer thank you email, a Slack message that says you saved us, that thing that everyone else relies on you for. Basically, receive. Because hiring managers don't hire for responsibilities, they hire proof. And if you wait until you're stressed to remember your proof, you forget half of it every single time. This is the mistake I see constantly. People sit down to write their resume only when they need a job and they're already overwhelmed and they're trying to magically remember three years of impact in one sitting. No wonder everything sounds generic. So instead, we flip it. We capture the wind when life is feeling calm and easy. If there's ever a time like that in your life. Here's exactly how I want you to set this up because simple is best. Open a plain work doc or Google Doc, nothing fancy, and create three quick sections. The first section is wins and results. This is where you jot down anything that went well, numbers, improvements, projects you completed, things you made better. The second section is problem solved. Because solving a problem is what companies actually pay you for and what they're going to look at when they want to hire you. Anytime you fix something, cleaned something up, prevented an issue, or made someone's life easier, this is a category it goes into. And the third section is proof. This is my favorite one. Copy and paste the receipts, performance review comments, thank you emails, Slack messages, metrics, screenshots, anything that backs you up that future you will forget. This section makes sure that you don't. That's it. Three messy sections. No formatting, no pressure. And here's my favorite part. Your brain bank is supposed to be messy. past sentences, random bullets, copy and paste notes, zero formatting, brain dump energy, my favorite kind. It's perfect because we can clean it up later. And honestly, this is where AI becomes incredibly helpful. You don't have to sit there trying to turn messy notes into beautiful résé bullet points by yourself anymore. That's not the highest use of your brain. What I do is dump my entire brag bank into AI along with the job description I'm targeting and ask it to help polish something simple like here are my career highlights. Create impactful results driven resume bullet points using metrics found when available tailored to this job description and then piece the job description right in. Now instead of starting from scratch, you're refining. It's faster, it's easier, and it takes so much pressure off you, especially when you're already stressed. There are honestly so many smart ways to use AI during a job search these days. I have a full long form video where I walk through how to level up your AI prompts, plus an AI prompt playbook that makes it super simple, and I'll link both in the comments for you. But here's the key thing, because this really matters. AI is the polish your bra is that thinking. If you skip the thinking and go straight to AI, you get generic garbage. If you feed it real receipts, you get gold. So don't wait until you need a job to start this. Make it tiny and consistent. Once a week, set a 5-minute timer and add one win, one result, and one problem you solve. This is what actually makes it stick and makes it easier when you need it. Because when something changes, a layoff, a restructure, or you just decide you're ready for something better, you're not staring at a blank page wondering what to say, you already have proof sitting there waiting for you. And that's what being layout ready means. Not panic, not scrambling, just being prepared and ready to go. If you found this helpful, make sure to follow and also check out my AI playbook below for more details into how to use AI strategically in a job search. Hope to see you next
